comparator.name: Bachelor Creative Technology
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 Creative Technology regulations confirm eight 15 EC modules, 30 EC of elective space and a 30 EC graduation semester. The example uses the Smart Technology specialisation and its sensor elective in module eight. The graduation project is completed in two parts worth 5 and 15 EC, alongside Academic Writing and Reflection.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Creative Technology bachelor. The current curriculum offers Smart Technology, Interactive Media and Designing Fair Futures as equally formal 15-EC specialisations and does not establish one as uniquely broad. Smart Technology is selected as the first option in the official order, independently of UCR fit.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad closest response is feasible. The official AI/data/smart-technology and human-centred interaction strands each support a coherent additional curriculum with material course consequences. All three pass qualitative and pairwise 30-EC distinctness, so production stops at the permitted maximum.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Introduction to Programming addresses the programming foundation inside this broad introductory module, without reproducing its full multidisciplinary scope.
Introduction to Data Science addresses data processing and visualisation, while the comparator module additionally physicalises data through an installation.
Machine Learning directly addresses the AI and machine-learning core, without the comparator's dedicated-hardware project.
Both study signals and systems. Twente also teaches circuits, electronics and sensors in this module.
Twente integrates programming, physical computing, circuits and visualisation in a smart-environment project.
Both frame problems around users and consider how ideas can become solutions. UCR focuses on entrepreneurship and value propositions.
Consumer Product Design directly develops user-needs analysis, prototyping and iterative evaluation, while the comparator focuses specifically on human-computer interaction.
Both ask students to consider the ethical and societal effects of technology. UCR focuses on artificial intelligence.
Both explore how creative choices shape an audience’s experience. UCR works through language, sound and performance, while Twente develops interactive installations.
Twente reserves 30 EC for approved electives, a minor or exchange.
Twente develops academic writing alongside the graduation project.
Twente requires an individual design and research project. UCR offers independent research separately.

notes.text: UCR offers related study in computing, product prototyping, cognition and communication. Twente integrates electronics, physical computing and interactive installations through a sequence of studio and laboratory projects.

audience.programmeDescription: Twente’s English-taught Creative Technology degree combines programming, electronics, human-centred design and interactive media. Students develop prototypes and installations, then complete an individual design and research project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The three UCR options explore creative computing and product design, AI and smart systems, or human interaction with technology. Twente connects physical computing, sensor work and interactive installations in dedicated project modules.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC example includes 30 EC of approved elective study and a 30 EC graduation semester.

componentNotes.m5-smart-technology: The example selects Smart Technology. Module eight includes its Sensor Technology in Sports unit.
componentNotes.y3-electives: Entry normally requires all 60 EC from year one and at least 30 EC from year two.
componentNotes.y3-project: Normally follows completion of modules 1–8. The 5 EC first part must be completed before the 15 EC second part.
